record_type_quote:
We performed a replication study about the relation of
cGKII gene to gout, and first demonstrated that the 4 cGKII
variants, rs11736177, rs10033237, rs7688672, and rs6837293,
had no significant association with gout susceptibility.

targets.authors: Chang SJ, Tsai MH, Ko YC, Tsai PC, Chen CJ, Lai HM.
targets.title: The cyclic GMP-dependent protein kinase II gene associates with gout disease: identified by genome-wide analysis and case-control study.
targets.evidence_quote:
The cGKII gene was located on 4q13.1-q21.1 and first
identified by Chang, et al to have an association with gout
in a Fukien-Taiwanese heritage population12.
targets.outcome_quote:
Among them, 4 SNP of cGKII
gene showed a significant association with gout12. However,
there are no replication studies indicating an association
between cGKII gene and gout in other ancestries. Our
present study revealed that the cGKII gene does not contribute to the gout susceptibility in a Japanese population. This
opposite result would be because of the difference in sample
size and population group between each study.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly contrast the original positive associations with the absent associations in their independent Japanese sample.

reasoning: Independent case-control sample re-tests four associations reported in Chang et al.; other genetic studies and methodological references are background.
